label: late original-phase inputs (t>=6), favoring l/3/r/g/2/x/h
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase at late positions: essentially none at t<=4, rate grows from t=5 to t=8 (21% of steps at t=8), so it is concentrated in long sequences (L=8,9 carry ~90% of mass) and at the last 1-3 inputs before <DEL>. Never fires during the copy phase and almost never at <DEL>. Within those late positions, firing depends strongly on the current input token: l, 3, r, g (and to a lesser degree 2, x, h) give the highest rates, and first occurrences of a token fire more than repeats. Rate is also higher when the sequence starts with a/v/j/u. Position plus token set captures ~75% of activation mass, but precision is only ~0.35: many late steps with these tokens stay silent, so the neuron likely responds to distributed hidden-state content that this predicate does not capture.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: l, 3, r, g, 2, x; least: v, m, a, j) and the first original token (most: a, v, j, u, c, i; least: 3, g, l, r); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, t=7, t=6.
